leads.consequence: On an existing LUKS/UKI install, an ordinary omarchy-settings upgrade replaces the disk copy of omarchy.script and removes the two old PNGs, but the boot image retains its previous copies. The next encrypted boot still shows the horizontal bar, potentially indefinitely if no later kernel rebuild or user-invoked omarchy plymouth set/refresh/reset occurs. A one-time image rebuild as part of upgrade/migration is needed, preserving any deliberately chosen unlock theme; note #10291's separate, unmerged migration runs only once and its refresh restores the stock theme.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at head `c10b4b9e`, the new fill parses and runs under the Plymouth 26.134.222 script plugin (the version named in the description). The crop geometry, z-order and alignment are exact. The password prompt (including the prompt re-shown after a wrong passphrase), shutdown, reboot and unencrypted-boot screens render pixel-identical to the parent. The fill stays aligned when a display is removed (through `layout()`) or added mid-progress. Removing `progress_bar.png` and `progress_box.png` leaves no remaining references, and the packaged directory copy removes them on upgrade. `plymouth-set-test.sh` passes 30/30, and the full shell suite shows the same failing files on base and head.

One visible issue: Plymouth's `Image.Crop` darkens translucent pixels, so the filled logo is not identical to the logo shown at the prompt on themes whose logo has a soft glow or antialiased edges.

### The cropped fill darkens translucent logo pixels

`position_fill()` draws `logo.image.Crop(...)`. In Plymouth 26.134.222, `image_crop` composites the source into a zeroed, transparent buffer (`src/plugins/splash/script/script-lib-image.c:134-151`). PNG images are premultiplied and never marked opaque, so the exact-copy fast path is skipped, and `blend_two_pixel_values` multiplies each translucent pixel's already premultiplied colour by alpha a second time (`src/libply-splash-core/ply-pixel-buffer.c:93-126`). Opaque pixels are copied exactly. An open upstream report, [plymouth work item 325](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/plymouth/plymouth/-/work_items/325), describes `Image.Crop` losing translucent pixels, and the crop and blend code is unchanged on Plymouth `main`.

Measured with the Plymouth 26.134.222 script plugin rendered offscreen (not a real DRM boot), comparing the 100% fill frame with the idle logo on each theme's background colour:

| Logo | Translucent pixels darkened | Mean / worst luminance drop |
|---|---|---|
| White | 106,522 of 107,021 | 18.0 / 39 |
| Tokyo Night | 176,051 of 176,519 | 12.0 / 31 |
| Vantablack | 106,522 of 107,021 | 10.6 / 23 |
| Lumon | 11,059 of 11,412 | 13.4 / 36.6 |
| 800x188 wordmark (default, Catppuccin, Catppuccin Latte, Flexoki Light) | 5,550 of 5,550 (antialiased edge) | 22.0 to 26.1 / 31.5 to 37.9 |

All opaque pixels match the idle logo, and nothing outside the logo box changes. For a single white pixel at alpha 128 on the default background, the screen shows `(140,141,146)` from the original image and `(76,77,82)` from the crop.

**Impact:** on White, the pink glow turns into a grey halo as the fill rises and stays grey at 100%. On Tokyo Night the glow is clearly weaker than at the prompt, and on Vantablack it is visibly weaker. On the wordmark themes only the 1 px antialiased edge changes, which is barely noticeable and consistent with the real-hardware boot described in the PR.

**Suggested change:** avoid cropping the logo. Keep the logo sprite at opacity 1 and cover the unfilled top rows with a background-coloured image at opacity 0.75. Over a solid background this gives the same 25% track (`0.75*bg + 0.25*(logo over bg)`), while the filled part is the real logo:

```text
PR:          logo @ 0.25  +  Crop(logo, bottom rows) @ 1      -> translucent pixels darkened
Alternative: logo @ 1     +  bg-colour image over top rows @ 0.75
```

A prototype of this variant rendered on default, Tokyo Night and White: the 100% frame is pixel-identical to the idle logo, the filled rows at 60% match the idle logo exactly, and the track rows are within 1 to 2 levels of the PR's track. The cost is a background-coloured asset that `omarchy-plymouth-set` would generate per theme (it already has `bg_hex` and runs `magick`), plus a packaged default and publish-list and test-allowlist entries. It relies on a single background colour, which `omarchy-plymouth-set` writes for both top and bottom. A smaller mitigation is to restore the logo to opacity 1 and hide the fill once progress reaches 1.0, which fixes only the finished state, and only when that final frame is drawn (see the timing note below).

### Overlap with open Plymouth PRs

#10799 (Caps Lock warning) edits the same lines: it adds `warning.png` next to `progress_box.png` in the publish list and test allowlist, adds it to the recolor loop that still names `progress_bar.png`, and adds a layout call beside the progress-box lines removed here. A trial merge conflicts in `bin/omarchy-plymouth-set`, `default/plymouth/omarchy.script` and `test/shell.d/plymouth-set-test.sh`. Whichever lands second needs to drop `progress_bar.png` from the recolor loop; `plymouth-set-test.sh` does not catch a stale entry there (see below). Draft #11579 (image optimisation) modifies both PNGs deleted here, so one of the two will hit modify/delete conflicts.

**Optional test improvement:** `plymouth-set-test.sh` stubs `magick` without checking that its input exists (`test/shell.d/plymouth-set-test.sh:291-296`), so a copy of this change with `progress_bar.png` left in the recolor loop still passes, while real `magick` would fail on the missing file and stop the theme switch. Checking that each recolor input exists in the stub would catch this.

**Optional:** while fake progress is rising, `position_fill()` re-crops the logo and redraws the filled area on every frame, even when the fill height has not changed. Of 369 measured frames, only 96 changed the screen for the default logo (261 for Tokyo Night). The cost was 0.24 ms per tick for the default logo and 1.48 ms for Tokyo Night, against 0.03 ms for the old bar: well inside the 20 ms frame budget. Skipping `SetImage` when `Math.Int(H * progress)` is unchanged would avoid about three quarters of the crops for the default logo and about 30% for Tokyo Night.

**On the open timing question:** source reading of Plymouth 26.134.222 shows that at quit it sends progress 1.0 and hides the splash about 10 ms later, while the script plugin draws on a 20 ms timer, so even the full logo is not guaranteed to be drawn. A partially filled logo at handoff is therefore possible regardless of `fake_progress_duration`. Separately, when a display is added mid-progress, plymouthd calls `display_normal` again and fake progress restarts from empty. The old bar resets the same way, but a whole logo emptying is more noticeable.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the diff, Plymouth 26.134.222 source and the `omarchy-settings` packaging. The base and head scripts were rendered frame by frame in isolated sandboxes with the Plymouth 26.134.222 script plugin, using a replacement in-memory display and timer (unlock on 8 shipped logos; wrong passphrase, display add and removal, shutdown and reboot on the default logo; unencrypted boot on default and Tokyo Night; plus synthetic images). Repository tests ran in the same sandboxes. Trial merges with related open PRs were done in disposable clones. No real boot, DRM output or LUKS unlock; HiDPI scaling and `updates` mode were not exercised; timings come from one machine and are indicative only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
